dedupe_keys.name: ogim oil and gas infrastructure mapping database

description: The Oil and Gas Infrastructure Mapping (OGIM) database is a global, spatially explicit and detailed data set of oil and gas infrastructure, built to support quantification and source attribution of methane emissions. It is developed by the Environmental Defense Fund and its subsidiary MethaneSAT, and version 3.0 was published on Zenodo in September 2026 by Madeleine O'Brien, Mark Omara, Anthony Himmelberger, Kaiya Weatherby and Ritesh Gautam. It integrates and quality-checks public geospatial data from governments, industry, academia and others into tables for production wells, offshore platforms, compressor stations, processing facilities, LNG facilities, crude oil refineries and pipelines. Version 3.0 adds 73 sources and updates 83, grows coverage from 150 to 193 countries and 7.6 million records, links production data to wells or leases in 20 US states, scores each record's data quality, and shows how satellite machine-learning detections can fill gaps. Coverage is global. The data are one GeoPackage of about 3.4 GB, downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: each record carries its source date, and some may be out of date. Simulation uses are hazard exposure of upstream and midstream assets, supply network models and methane studies. Related records: data-gem-global-oil-and-gas-extraction-tracker and data-gem-global-gas-infrastructure-tracker track projects at a coarser level.
